headline: Isoform-resolved RNA-seq tools dissect splicing, polyadenylation and intronic transcripts
label: Isoform Resolved Transcriptome Tooling
summary: Recent preprints and publications extend transcript-level RNA-seq analysis from isolated event calling toward integrated, multi-layer resources.
synthesis: The common thread is resolving transcript-level structure from RNA-seq for downstream interpretation. splicelogic converts transcript-set differences into discrete splicing events, and MOCHI curates candidate independent intronic transcripts from strand-specific short-read data. Alternative polyadenylation is addressed by scPolyA in single-cell and spatial 3' transcriptomes and by IsoAPA, a long-read atlas of 2.3M transcript-resolved polyadenylation sites across 816 sample groups. Isoform diversity is treated as a complementary expression dimension across 4,814 GTEx samples, and a mouse atlas links age-associated differential transcript usage across brain, liver and adipose to predominantly regulatory isoform switching. R2T2P connects genome-guided assembly to translation profiling and proteomics. The newer element is movement toward integrated resources. An AlphaGenome promoter perturbation study offers a cautionary counterpoint, with CAGE and RNA-seq predictions decoupling and weak propagation to downstream exons.
